The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with small yellowish-green spots/speckling scattered across the surface, some marginal browning, and an overall dark green leaf. This narrows candidates to leaf diseases.

Top candidates from visual inspection: Powdery Mildew, Leaf Mold, Bacterial Speck, Septoria Leaf Blotch. Let me check reference images one at a time.
Powdery mildew shows distinct white powdery circular patches - doesn't match the test image's scattered yellow speckling. Next: Leaf Mold.
Leaf Mold shows large olive/tan blotchy spots - doesn't match. Next: Bacterial Speck.
Doesn't match - Bacterial Speck has large dark spots with distortion. Next: Cucumber Mosaic Virus.
CMV shows distorted shoestring leaves - not matching. Next: Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (bronzing + small spots).
TSWV shows ring-spot/concentric patterns - not matching. Next: another Powdery Mildew reference (yellow lesion stage).
This Powdery Mildew shows white dusty coating - partially similar to the test image's texture. For my final view, Septoria Leaf Blotch.

Septoria shows distinct circular gray/tan spots with dark borders - not matching the fine yellow speckling in the test image.

**Summary of comparisons:**
- Powdery Mildew (CDDM_78): Dark green leaf with dusty/whitish-yellow surface coating — closest visual match to the test image's scattered yellowish speckling on dark green leaf
- Leaf Mold (CDDM_313): Larger blotchy olive spots on yellowed leaf — doesn't match
- Bacterial Speck: Large dark spots with distortion — doesn't match
- CMV: Distorted shoestring leaves — doesn't match
- TSWV: Ring-spot concentric patterns — doesn't match
- Septoria: Circular gray spots with dark borders — doesn't match

The test image shows a dark green tomato leaf with small scattered yellowish-white speckling and a somewhat dusty surface texture. This is most consistent with Powdery Mildew's early yellow lesion stage, where light-green to bright yellow lesions appear before the dense white powdery coating forms. The CDDM_78 reference showing a dark green leaf with powdery/dusty surface appearance is the closest visual match.
